assertions.description: Suspicious-site warnings expose no runtime surface to pages: no Safe-Browsing-related own property exists on navigator or window. Absence is the contract — a page must never be able to observe the user's protection level or a warning verdict.
assertions.test: (()=>{ for (const obj of [navigator, window]) { for (const name of Object.getOwnPropertyNames(obj)) { if (/safebrowsing|suspicious|sitewarning/i.test(name)) return false; } } return true; })()

assertions.description: Under Safe Browsing Enhanced protection in Chrome 152, a site with signals of potential maliciousness triggers a bypassable pop-up warning that must be clicked through before continuing; Standard protection shows no warning for unconfirmed signals.
assertions.test: Requires Chrome 152 with Enhanced protection and a URL Safe Browsing scores as suspicious: verify the pop-up appears, is bypassable, and does not appear under Standard protection for the same URL.

assertions.description: The red full-page interstitial continues to be shown for confirmed malicious sites at every Safe Browsing level — the new pop-up tier is additive, not a replacement.
assertions.test: Requires a confirmed blocklisted test URL: verify the red interstitial (not the pop-up) is shown under both Standard and Enhanced protection.

assertions.description: A page cannot detect that its visitor bypassed a suspicious-site warning: navigation timing and referrer carry no warning marker.
assertions.test: Requires the warning to fire on a controlled origin: after click-through, inspect document.referrer, performance navigation entries, and request headers for any warning artifact — there must be none.
